Bug_Title: REFLF: Public method uses reflection to modify a field it gets in its parameter which could increase the accessibility of any class (REFLF_REFLECTION_MAY_INCREASE_ACCESSIBILITY_OF_FIELD)
Bug_Details:
SEI CERT SEC05-J rule forbids the use of reflection to increase accessibility of classes, methods or fields. If
a class in a package provides a public method which takes an instance of java.lang.reflect.Field as its
parameter and calls a setter (or setAccessible()) method then it increases accessibility of fields in the same
package which are private, protected or package private. An attacker code may call this method and pass such
field to change it. This should be avoided by either making the method non-public or by checking for package
access permission on the package.
Bug_Explanation: The public method 'modifyField' uses reflection to modify the accessibility of a field. It takes a 'Field' object as a parameter and calls 'setAccessible(true)' on it, which could increase the accessibility of private, protected, or package-private fields in any class within the package. This violates the SEC05-J rule and could lead to unintended access to sensitive fields.
Trigger_Explanation: The trigger occurs because the testShowBug test case calls the showBug method, which internally calls the modifyField method. The modifyField method uses reflection to modify the accessibility of a field by calling setAccessible(true) on a Field object, thereby violating the security rule. The test case tries to validate the change of a private field's accessibility and modification, leading to failure due to the SEC05-J rule violation.
